name: Everbloom

stars.name: Everbloom
stars.notes: Near-perfect Sol analog, remarkably stable luminosity output conducive to long-term biosphere development

planets.name: Cinderbed
planets.notes: Tidally locked, molten dayside with crystallized nightside minerals prized by jewelers.

planets.name: Solace
planets.notes: Primary paradise colony, 70% tropical and temperate forest coverage, population 6.2 billion. Indigenous megaflora reach heights exceeding 300 meters.

planets.name: Tidesong
planets.notes: Warm global ocean teeming with bioluminescent life, floating arcology settlements, population 1.8 billion.

planets.name: Fernreach
planets.notes: Cool temperate world with continent-spanning fern forests and alpine meadows, population 420 million. Research-focused colony studying indigenous fauna.

planets.name: Colossarion
planets.notes: Banded emerald-green giant, its radiation belts shield the inner system from charged particles. Three moons host research outposts.

planets.name: Palefrost
planets.notes: Subsurface ocean detected beneath 40km ice shell. Unmanned probes have found microbial life in hydrothermal vent systems.

planets.name: Farwander
planets.notes: Distant ice dwarf with a highly eccentric orbit, likely a captured rogue body.

asteroid_belts.name: The Pollen Ring
asteroid_belts.notes: Named for its golden color when viewed from Fernreach. Contains organic compounds of unknown origin.

stations.name: Canopy Station
stations.notes: Primary trade hub, strict biosecurity protocols to protect Solace's ecosystem. All imports undergo decontamination.

stations.name: Tidesong Orbital
stations.notes: Coordinates floating city logistics and manages marine conservation zones across the planet.

stations.name: Bloomwatch
stations.notes: Xenobiology research center cataloging Fernreach's unique cold-adapted fauna.

stations.name: Deepgreen Relay
stations.notes: Long-range communications relay and early warning station for inbound traffic.

faction_control.notes: Democratic eco-governance coalition dedicated to sustainable development. Strict environmental regulations limit industrial activity on all inhabited worlds.

history: First surveyed in 2241 by the exploration vessel Greenmantle, which reported three worlds with independent biospheres—an unprecedented discovery that drew immediate scientific attention.

The Everbloom Conservancy was established in 2259 as a governing charter explicitly prioritizing ecological preservation alongside colonization, making it one of the first systems with constitutional environmental protections.
Today Everbloom is considered humanity's greatest natural treasure, attracting millions of visitors annually and serving as the model for sustainable colonial development across known space.
description: Everbloom is a system that defies probability. Orbiting a near-perfect solar twin, three worlds independently evolved complex biospheres, each with unique biochemistry that shares only the most fundamental molecular building blocks. Solace's towering megaflora forests create cathedral-like canopies visible from orbit, while Tidesong's bioluminescent oceans pulse with light patterns that some xenobiologists believe constitute a form of planetary-scale communication. Even cold Fernreach hosts fern forests that stretch from pole to pole, their fronds swaying in winds that carry spores across entire continents.

The system's significance extends far beyond scientific curiosity. Everbloom has become humanity's most cherished paradise colony—a place where people come to remember what living worlds look and feel like. The Conservancy's strict environmental laws mean that cities on Solace are woven into the forest canopy rather than built upon cleared ground. Tidesong's floating arcologies drift with ocean currents, and Fernreach's research settlements leave minimal footprints. Heavy interstellar traffic flows through Canopy Station, where biosecurity officers ensure not a single invasive microbe reaches the worlds below.

Yet paradise carries its own tensions. The Conservancy's regulations frustrate mining interests that covet the Pollen Ring's organic compounds. Palefrost's subsurface microbial life has sparked fierce debate over whether to permit crewed exploration of its hidden ocean. And the deepest mystery remains unanswered: how did three worlds in one system each develop life independently? Some researchers whisper about ancient seeding, pointing to the Pollen Ring's inexplicable organic chemistry as evidence. The truth, if it exists, lies buried beneath canopy, ocean, and ice.
